title: Issue reads silently drop comments past the first 50 (no first:, no paging, in the Linear issue-detail query)
description:
## Goal

An issue read returns all of the issue's comments, or says plainly that it didn't. Today it silently drops everything past the first page.

## Context

`API_ISSUE_DETAIL_QUERY` (`lib/providers/linear/index.js`, around lines 1505–1535) asks for `comments { nodes { … } }` with no `first:` argument and no paging. Linear then returns its default page of 50, with no sign that more exist.

Seen in use: `GET /api/proxy/issues/LIN-4150` returns exactly **50** comments, though LIN-4150 holds many more. The paper `docs/papers/harbour/cleaner-than-it-started.md` (LIN-4315) found that, because of this, every Survey comment posted to LIN-4150 before 5 Nov 02:58 is invisible through the proxy. The paper's freeze had to assert the comments it needed were inside the 50. It names this as a Harbour defect in the class of LIN-3309 and LIN-4068. `children`, `relations` and `inverseRelations` in the same query have the same shape.

## This step

* **Read every comment.** The issue read pages through comments (`first:` plus `pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor }`) until it has them all. A page-size choice and a sensible upper bound are the builder's call; if a bound is hit, the response says the list is truncated rather than going silent.
* **Same for the other lists:** `children`, `relations` and `inverseRelations` in that query, where they can exceed a page.
* **Pin it with a test** using a fake provider page of more than 50.
* **Document it** where the proxy's `GET /issues/{id}` is described: complete, or flagged as truncated.

**Not this ticket:** other providers' issue reads, unless they share this query.

## Done when

* A test shows more than 50 comments returned, in order.
* A truncated response is flagged, not silent.
* `GET /api/proxy/issues/LIN-4150` returns more than 50 comments.

## At merge

* The check exists, and every unbounded connection is fixed or listed with its reason.
* `fetchIssueComments` pages.
* The flag reaches the wire.
* The order holds across a page boundary.
* `GET /api/proxy/issues/LIN-4150` returns more than 50 comments, once deployed.

## Implementation Plan

**Implemented as approved** in [https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2332](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2332>) (merged as `badec1fb`): one `pageConnection` helper used by `issueDetail`, `relations()` and `fetchIssueComments` (the gate throws at the cap), a top-level `truncated` flag that survives `flattenIssue`, a gql-only source check for unbounded connections, and the docs. No deviations from the plan; the review's close-out fixes are listed in the close-out comment. The Survey notes, plan decisions, witness list and failure analysis that were here are preserved in the task snapshots and the comment trail.

### Session fit and review

fits one session. One helper, three call sites, one flag, one check, two doc files; each lands and is verified on its own in that order: check (red) → helper + tests → apply to the three reads → route/docs.

plan-review due: yes (it changes what the merge/Done gate reads and makes it throw at the cap, which is a merge-rule change; a second reader should look at decision 4).

comments.body:
## Survey global: LIN-4322 @ 5c63aa261

**Where it lands.** `lib/providers/linear/index.js` (2,374 lines). `API_ISSUE_DETAIL_QUERY` (1505) feeds `issueDetail` (1893), then `routes/proxy-reads.js:214`, which sorts comments and calls `flattenIssue` (`lib/proxy-wire.js:303`). This area is better than it was (LIN-308, LIN-3569). But this file keeps fixing this defect class one query at a time, with a different number each time: `history(last: 50)` (LIN-1074), `comments(first: 250)` (LIN-3309), `children(first: 101)` plus `CHILDREN_READ_CAP` (LIN-4068). None of these pages; each picks a bigger bound. The file has no helper for paging a nested connection; its only paging loop, `fetchProjects` (775), pages top-level `issues`.

**Done the obvious way.** Someone adds a fourth local loop inside `issueDetail`, and the file now has four answers to the same question. Two traps:
- **The flag can get lost.** `flattenIssue` turns `{ nodes }` into a bare array and throws away everything else on the connection. A `truncated` set beside `nodes` would vanish before it reached the wire, and nothing would notice. The flag has to sit at the top level of the issue. Existing convention: `truncated` only when true (`github/client.js:82`).
- **Docs live in two places.** `docs/proxy-integration.md` §Get Issue Detail (~770) and the served catalogue `lib/proxy-instructions.js:129–145` both describe the detail shape. If only one is updated, they disagree. The `local` provider's `issueDetail` builds the same shape and would also need to carry, or deliberately leave out, the new field.

**This ticket targets a symptom.** The same un-paged shape exists in two sibling queries in the same file. Both are still un-paged after this ticket unless it is widened:
- `ISSUE_COMMENTS_QUERY` (1074) → `fetchIssueComments`. `lib/close-out-readiness.js:77` reads it, then takes `latestReviewComment(comments)` and `parseRunLedger` from it. Those are the review verdict and the ledger that gate merge and Done. On a trail longer than 50, the *latest* review may not be among the 50 comments returned. Worse than the proxy's failure: a stale verdict, not a missing one. `lib/ci-wake-sweep.js:336` uses the same read.
- `RELATIONS_QUERY` (1356) → `GET /issues/{id}/relations`. It has the same `relations` / `inverseRelations` shape that this ticket fixes in the detail query.

**Better, at a cost this task can carry.** Write one helper that drains an issue's nested connection: a follow-up `issue(id){ <field>(first:, after:) { nodes pageInfo } }` with a page size and a cap, returning `{ nodes, truncated }`. Use it for the four lists in `issueDetail`. Then point `fetchIssueComments` and `RELATIONS_QUERY` at the same helper. Same provider, same shape, so the "other providers" exclusion doesn't apply; each is a few lines. Test the helper once with a fake page of more than 50, in the existing `GraphQLClient.prototype.request` stub style (`tests/unit/linear-provider-api.test.js:59`). Add one route test showing the flag survives `flattenIssue`. If the siblings aren't taken, at minimum file a ticket for `fetchIssueComments`, because close-out depends on it.

**Better still, not this task.** Move the deliberate fail-closed bounds (LIN-3309's 250, LIN-4068's 101, `history(last: 50)`) in the prompt-context `ISSUE_DETAIL_QUERY` onto the same helper. Those bounds are deliberate and feed prompt rendering and the subtree index. That migration is also the natural place for a test that fails whenever a Linear query here selects a connection with no `first:`/`last:`. Today the next unbounded connection would go as unnoticed as this one did.

## Survey open-0: LIN-4322 @ 5c63aa261

**The ticket points at one query, but the problem is wider.** The LinearViewer Linear provider sets `first:` by hand on each connection, and it has done that one ticket at a time (LIN-1074 `history(last: 50)`, LIN-3309 `comments(first: 250)`, LIN-4068 `children(first: 101)`). These connections in `lib/providers/linear/index.js` still have no bound at all:
- `API_ISSUE_DETAIL_QUERY` (1505): children, comments, relations, inverseRelations. This is the ticket.
- `ISSUE_COMMENTS_QUERY` (1074), used by `fetchIssueComments`. It feeds `readCloseOutChain` (`lib/close-out-readiness.js:77`: PR URLs and `latestReviewComment`, which gate merge/Done), `run-evidence.js:235` and `ci-wake-sweep.js:336`. On a long trail the close-out gate silently reads 50, which matters more than the proxy read.
- `FOCUSED_CHILD_QUERY` comments (~1056), `RELATIONS_QUERY` (1356, which backs `GET /issues/{id}/relations`), and the `inverseRelations` at 415 in the context query.

Same provider, so in scope by the ticket's rule. Without a shared helper, each later fix repeats this one.

**Why it's harder than adding `first:`**
1. **Paging nested connections takes extra requests.** The cursor sits inside `issue(id){ comments(...) }`, so pages 2+ need a follow-up query per connection, keyed on the UUID resolved by the first call. Use one generic `pageConnection(client, issueId, field, selection)`, not four loops. Guard against a repeated `endCursor`.
2. **The wire shape has nowhere to put a flag.** `flattenIssue` (`lib/proxy-wire.js:326-388`) turns `{nodes}` into plain arrays, which drops `pageInfo`. A truncation signal has to be a sibling field (for example `truncated: { comments: true }`) that gets through `flattenIssue`. The Local provider's `issueDetail` (`tests/unit/local-provider.test.js:282`) has to emit the same shape, with nothing truncated. Agree on the field name before any code.
3. **Ordering is unclear in the repo itself.** LIN-1074's note says forward paging returns the *oldest* N. The paper cited by the ticket found the comments *before* 5 Nov 02:58 were the ones missing, which means the newest were kept. Don't rely on either. Pass `orderBy: createdAt` explicitly, keep the route's local sort (`routes/proxy-reads.js:225`), and test "in order" across a page boundary.
4. **The test stub ignores variables.** `stub()` in `tests/unit/linear-provider-api.test.js:59` returns one fixed response. The >50 test needs a stub that branches on `after`. Existing fixtures return `comments: {nodes}` with no `pageInfo`, so a missing `pageInfo` must mean "done". Otherwise those tests loop forever.
5. **There's no doc block to amend.** `lib/proxy-instructions.js` never spells out the `GET /issues/{id}` response. It only refers to it (163, 758, 797). Choose proxy-instructions or `docs/proxy-integration.md` first.
6. **Cost per read.** Linear limits by query complexity. Page at ~100 and cap at ~1,000 (about 10 requests for LIN-4150).

**What I'd do first**
Write a provider-level `pageConnection` helper with its test (stub branches on `after`, 120 fake comments, then 1,000+ to hit the cap and get the flag). Apply it to `issueDetail` and `fetchIssueComments` in the same change. It's the same defect on the gating path, and a one-line reuse. Fix the `truncated` field on the wire and in the docs before touching the route. Leave FOCUSED_CHILD and RELATIONS_QUERY as named follow-ups if the diff grows.

Done-when check: LIN-4150's `.comments|length` > 50.

### Plan Review Verdict

**Verdict:** Approve. The premise is right, the scope covers the cause (no way to page a nested connection, and no check), and the safeguards hold on the paths that write merge/Done. Four notes below; one of them corrects a claim in decision 4.

**What I checked, on `main` at `90542b2c`.** Nothing in the touched files has changed since the plan's `5c63aa26`. The only commit since then is test-only (LIN-4311).
- `API_ISSUE_DETAIL_QUERY` (1505–1535), `ISSUE_COMMENTS_QUERY` (1074) and `RELATIONS_QUERY` (1356) all select connections with no `first:`. `issueDetail` (1893) returns `data.issue` raw.
- `flattenIssue` (`lib/proxy-wire.js:303`) unwraps `children`/`comments`/`relations`/`inverseRelations` and leaves unknown top-level keys alone. A top-level `truncated` survives, as the plan says. Its route test is still the right witness.
- The route sorts comments locally (`routes/proxy-reads.js:225`). `lib/proxy-instructions.js:129–145` does restate the detail shape, as the plan says (the ticket was wrong on that). The relations shape is at `:186–190`.
- The stub style at `tests/unit/linear-provider-api.test.js:59` gets `(query, variables)`, so a stub that branches on `after` works.

**Notes for the builder** (none blocks):

1. **Decision 4's "fails closed … loosens none" is true for the writes, not for every caller.** I traced what a throw from `fetchIssueComments` becomes on each path:
   - `routes/workspace-api-run-evidence.js:272` (person's PR check, which writes Done): an error response. **Closed.** ✓
   - `lib/close-out-merges.js:143` (pipeline Done): the catch at :180 returns `none`, so no merge is recorded. **Closed.** ✓
   - `closeOutNotReady` (`lib/close-out-readiness.js:125`, used by `dispatch-entrance.js:1329` and `workspace-api-run-evidence.js:349`): the catch at :141 **admits**. This fail-open is deliberate and logged ("guard read failed, admitting"). So past the cap, this guard admits blind instead of judging on a prefix.
   - Callers that are not gates: `/workspace/:urlKey/api/comments/:issueId` (`routes/workspace-api-issue-read.js:49`, the dashboard Comments toggle) returns an error. `routes/dashboard.js:494` (PR state) and `routes/dashboard-effort.js:96` (skip) fail, and `ci-wake-sweep.js:336` records "unreadable". Each of these wants the latest entries too, so an error is still more honest than a prefix.

   Nothing here changes the plan's decision: the paths that write merge/Done refuse, and the guard's fail-open policy is existing house policy, outside this ticket. Do two things:
   - In the PR, list these outcomes instead of "loosens none".
   - Add one assertion to the gate witness: `readCloseOutChain` rejects when the read throws at the cap. That is what `close-out-merges` and the check route rely on.

2. **The check's hit list is larger than the plan expects. Scope the scan to `gql` templates.** A rough scan for `field(args?) { nodes` with no `first:`/`last:` finds about 40 hits. It also finds three false positives in plain JS after the templates (1817, 1877), so the check must parse only inside the `gql` backtick bodies. Beyond the three in scope and the two named follow-ups, the hits that can plausibly go past 50 and need a filed follow-up (do not widen the diff) are:
   - `ISSUE_DETAIL_FIELDS_QUERY` `comments` (338): the dashboard detail gallery and task-edit page. This is the same comments defect on another surface.
   - The prompt-context `ISSUE_DETAIL_QUERY`'s unbounded `children` (parent's children = siblings, ~546; grandchildren ~502/528/572) and the `relations`/`inverseRelations` under them. These sit next to LIN-4068's bounded `children(first: 101)`, but they are not themselves bounded.
   - `ISSUE_FIELDS_FRAGMENT` / `_SLIM_FRAGMENT` `relations` (114/164): the dashboard tree.
   - `CYCLE_DETAIL_QUERY` `issues` (1321), `LABELS_QUERY` `issueLabels` (1337), `CYCLES_QUERY(_ALL)`, `STATES_QUERY`, `TEAMS_QUERY`, `PROJECTS_QUERY`/`API_PROJECTS_QUERY`. These are top-level reads, so they are not issue reads, but the check will flag them.

   The plan's triage rule already covers all of these. The list is here so the builder starts from it. Labels lists can carry a reason ("an issue's labels").

3. **Do not let the docs say which end gets cut until it has been seen live.** Decision 3 says forward paging keeps "the oldest 1,000". The plan also says to rely on neither the LIN-1074 note nor the paper, and those two disagree. The stubs cannot settle it. Before writing "the first 1,000 by creation time" in either doc, check it once against live Linear: page LIN-4150 with `first: 5, orderBy: createdAt` and look at the dates. Otherwise word the docs neutrally ("`truncated.comments` means the list was cut at N; the route returns what was read, oldest first"). The gate throws either way, so only the docs depend on this.

4. **The follow-up query needs an id it can address.** `ISSUE_COMMENTS_QUERY` and `RELATIONS_QUERY` do not select `id`. `issue(id:)` takes either a UUID or an identifier, so passing the caller's `issueId` through is fine; selecting `id` and using that also works. Either way, the follow-up must not read `data.issue.id` from a query that never selected it. Also use one `client.request` call form inside the helper: the file uses both `(doc, vars)` and `({ document, variables, signal })` (806). The stub must match whichever you pick.

**Smaller points.**
- The plan already names the complexity risk, and its live check (LIN-4150 plus a small issue) is the right witness. Keep `first: 100` and add no fields.
- Children are passed through `flattenIssue` recursively, so a child never carries `truncated`. That is fine.
- `Local.relations()` (`lib/providers/local/index.js:464`) should, like `issueDetail`, carry no `truncated`. Pin that with the same test.

**Hand-off:** to `implementation` with the notes above.

## LIN-4322: PR open, CI green

PR: https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2332 (branch `feat/lin-4322-paginate-linear-nested-connections`, commit `88addda6`).

- `pageConnection` pages nested issue connections (`first: 100, orderBy: createdAt`, cap 1,000). A cut list is flagged as a top-level `truncated` object, present only when something was cut.
- `issueDetail`, `relations()` and `fetchIssueComments` (the close-out gate) page their lists. The gate throws at the cap rather than return a prefix.
- Source-level check for unbounded gql connections. Remaining hits are allowlisted with reasons and follow-ups LIN-4325 to LIN-4328.
- CI: unit tests, four E2E shards, secret scan and CI success all pass.

Not yet verified: live Linear accepting `orderBy` on these connections within its complexity limit. Check `GET /api/proxy/issues/LIN-4150` returns more than 50 comments once deployed.

## Review — LIN-4322

PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2332, head `88addda644509e042daa71e11736e3407a27b119` (one commit on `main` @ `90542b2c`).

CI: green on head `88addda6`: Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4, Secret scan, CI success. I also re-ran `npm run test:unit` on the head myself: 23,940 pass, 0 fail.

**Scope against the plan.** The diff stays in the planned places: the provider, `routes/proxy-reads.js` (relations only), the two docs, and tests. Nothing in the touched files has changed on `main` since the ticket was created. The recent history of `lib/providers/linear/index.js` shows no reverted or re-applied change to these queries. The code follows the plan's decisions 1–5:
- One `pageConnection`, used at the three call sites, with `first: 100, orderBy: createdAt` and a cap of 1,000.
- It terminates on missing `pageInfo`, on a null or repeated `endCursor`, and at the cap.
- `truncated` sits at the top level and is present only when true.
- `fetchIssueComments` throws at the cap.
- The gql-only source check has a reasoned allowlist.
- Follow-ups LIN-4325 to LIN-4328 exist.

The code is correct. The gaps are in the witnesses and docs that the approved plan and plan review asked for.

**Mutation checks** (each reverted afterwards):
- `fetchIssueComments` with its throw disabled → red (1 fail). ✓
- `orderBy: createdAt` removed from the follow-up query only → red (1 fail). ✓
- **The relations route's `...(issueRelations.truncated ? …)` line deleted → still green (1,336 pass, 0 fail).** Nothing tests that the flag reaches the wire on `GET /issues/{id}/relations`.
- The detail route's flag is pinned only through a direct `flattenIssue(issueDetail(...))` call, not through the route. The plan's route witness ("comments sorted even when the provider returns pages out of order") is not there.

**Gaps against the plan and plan review:**
1. **Docs say which end is cut. Plan-review note 3 said not to, unless checked live.** `docs/proxy-integration.md` (both new paragraphs) says "read whole, oldest first by creation time, up to 1,000", which implies the newest are cut. Nobody checked this against live Linear. The stubs cannot settle it.
2. **Relations-route witness missing** (the mutation above) **and detail-route witness missing** (plan § Witnesses, "Route").
3. **`readCloseOutChain` rejects at the cap: not asserted.** Plan-review note 1 asked for this; it is what `close-out-merges` and the run-evidence route rely on.
4. **Local provider pin missing.** No test asserts that Local's `issueDetail` and `relations()` carry no `truncated` (plan decision 6, plan-review smaller points).
5. **The PR body does not list the throw outcomes per caller** (plan-review note 1). In particular, `closeOutNotReady` (`lib/close-out-readiness.js:141`) admits by its existing fail-open policy when the read throws at the cap. The PR body should say so.
6. **Hardening (small).** `pageConnection`'s final `return { nodes: nodes.slice(0, CONNECTION_CAP), truncated: false }` would silently cut if a page ever came back with more than 100 nodes. Unreachable with `first: 100` today, but it goes against the helper's own doc comment ("never returned as if whole").

**Isolated, or one of a class?** One of a class: "a Linear issue read's nested connection stops silently at the default 50". The source check enumerates the class, and every remaining hit is allowlisted with a reason.

### What CI Did Not Prove
- **Inside (the ticket's own done-when):** live Linear accepts `orderBy: createdAt` with `first: 100` on all four nested connections in one query, within its complexity limit. If it does not, *every* issue read breaks, not just long ones.
  - **After the deploy:** `GET /api/proxy/issues/LIN-4150` returns `.comments | length` > 50 and no `truncated`, and a small issue (e.g. LIN-4322) still returns 200 with its comments. Also `GET /api/proxy/issues/LIN-4150/relations` returns 200.
  - **Rollback:** revert `88addda6`. It is reversible: no migration, no persisted shape, and `truncated` is additive.
- **Inside (the docs claim, decision 3):** which end live Linear cuts under `orderBy: createdAt` forward paging.
  - **Before the merge:** reword the docs neutrally (fix 1 below).
  - **After the deploy:** check once by paging LIN-4150 and comparing the first and last `createdAt` of the 50+ list against the issue's earliest and latest comments. Only then may the docs name an end.
- **Inside (the plan's witnesses):** the relations route and detail route carry `truncated`; `readCloseOutChain` rejects at the cap; Local emits no `truncated`. **Before the merge**, by fixes 2–4 below. The distinguishing check: each new test goes red when its code path is removed (for the relations route, delete the `...(issueRelations.truncated …)` spread).
- **Inside, dropped with a reason (the approved plan, decision 5, and the allowlist):**
  - Prompt-context `ISSUE_DETAIL_QUERY` children, relations and inverseRelations, plus `FOCUSED_CHILD_QUERY.comments`. Reason: the bound is a prompt-rendering decision, not a drain (LIN-4325 tracks it).
  - `ISSUE_DETAIL_FIELDS_QUERY.comments` (attachment gallery) and `ISSUE_FIELDS_FRAGMENT` / `_SLIM_FRAGMENT` relations (dashboard tree). Reason: the plan's triage rule, "do not widen this diff". LIN-4326 and LIN-4327 track them.

  These are the same defect class. They are settled by this explicit drop, not by the filed tickets. Close-out records the drop in its comment. Nothing more is needed unless the person overrides it.
- **Outside:** `CYCLE_DETAIL_QUERY.issues` and the workspace-level lists (projects, cycles, issueLabels). These are top-level reads, not nested issue connections. Already filed as LIN-4326 and LIN-4328, so nothing more for close-out.

### Fixes for close-out to make (no new design)
1. `docs/proxy-integration.md` §Get Issue Detail: replace "each read whole, oldest first by creation time, up to 1,000 items per list. A list that reaches that cap is cut there" with "each read whole, up to 1,000 items per list (requested `orderBy: createdAt`; the route returns comments oldest first). A list that reaches that cap is cut". In §relations, drop "oldest first," the same way.
2. In a route test (the style of the existing proxy-reads route tests), use a fake provider whose `relations()` returns `truncated: { inverseRelations: true }` and assert that the JSON body has the top-level `truncated`. Likewise, use a fake `issueDetail` returning comments out of order plus `truncated: { comments: true }`, and assert that the body's `truncated` is present and its comments are sorted ascending.
3. `tests/unit/close-out-readiness-chain.test.js` (or the paging test): with `fetchIssueComments` stubbed over CONNECTION_CAP+1, `readCloseOutChain` rejects.
4. `tests/unit/local-provider.test.js`: assert `'truncated' in await issueDetail(...) === false` and the same for `relations(...)`.
5. Add a short "throw outcomes per caller" list to the PR body, from plan-review note 1, including `closeOutNotReady` admitting by its existing fail-open policy.
6. `lib/providers/linear/index.js` `pageConnection` final return: `return { nodes: nodes.slice(0, CONNECTION_CAP), truncated: nodes.length > CONNECTION_CAP }`.

### Verdict
Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger. The implementation is correct, and the reads at the gate fail closed. What remains are named witnesses, the neutral docs wording the plan review required, and the live LIN-4150 check after deploy (rollback: revert `88addda6`).

## Close-out — LIN-4322

**Merged:** https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2332, squash `badec1fb7a1b3c7ed017ee1ce051215c06a21613`, pinned with `--match-head-commit 97cd2425434bff769a153a8bd902e44db3b54f43`. Review verdict was Approve (conditional on the ledger below).

**CI on the merged head `97cd2425`:** Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4, Secret scan, CI success all pass, read fresh before the merge. Locally, `npm run test:unit` gave 23,947 pass, 0 fail.

### Changes I made after the approval (commit `97cd2425`, each answers a review fix)
1. **Fix 1, docs:** `docs/proxy-integration.md` no longer says which end a cut list loses. It names the requested `orderBy: createdAt` and the route's oldest-first comment sort; "oldest first" is dropped from the relations paragraph.
2. **Fix 2, route witnesses:** new `tests/unit/proxy-truncated-routes.test.js`. `GET /issues/:id` returns the top-level `truncated` and sorts out-of-order comments ascending. `GET /issues/:id/relations` returns `truncated` beside `trashed`. Both omit the key when nothing was cut.
3. **Fix 3, gate witness:** `close-out-readiness-chain.test.js`: `readCloseOutChain` rejects over the real Linear `fetchIssueComments` with CONNECTION_CAP+1 comments (not a stub that throws by itself).
4. **Fix 4, Local pin:** `local-provider.test.js`: `issueDetail` and `relations` carry no `truncated` key.
5. **Fix 5, PR body:** per-caller throw outcomes added, including `closeOutNotReady` admitting by its existing fail-open policy.
6. **Fix 6, hardening:** `pageConnection` now returns `truncated: nodes.length > CONNECTION_CAP` on its final slice, with a test for an oversized first page.

Witness checks, each reverted after: gate throw disabled → 2 red; relations `truncated` spread deleted → 1 red; detail comment sort removed → 1 red; hardening reverted → 1 red (the oversized-page test). Nothing here was a new design.

### Ledger
- **Live Linear accepts `orderBy: createdAt` + `first: 100` on all four lists (inside), settled after deploy:** `GET /api/proxy/issues/LIN-4150` now returns **143** comments (was exactly 50), sorted ascending, 143 unique ids, `createdAt` 2026-11-02T21:44:55Z → 2026-11-06T12:02:19Z, no `truncated` key. `GET /issues/LIN-4150/relations` 200 (keys `inverseRelations, relations, trashed`). `GET /issues/LIN-4322` 200 with its 5 comments, no `truncated`. Observed when the deploy landed (about 12:05 UTC; the same probe returned 50 until then). **Rollback (named by review):** revert `88addda6` (squashed into `badec1fb`); no migration, `truncated` is additive.
- **Which end live Linear cuts (inside):** **not run, and cannot be run here.** No live list reaches the 1,000 cap (the largest is LIN-4150 at 143), so a cut cannot be observed. The docs stay neutral as review directed. Who can run it: anyone with an issue holding more than 1,000 comments, or a `first: 5, orderBy: createdAt` probe against Linear directly; I have only the proxy.
- **Plan witnesses (inside):** done by fixes 2–4 above, each shown red when its code path is removed.
- **Dropped with a reason (inside, per review):** prompt-context `ISSUE_DETAIL_QUERY` children/relations/inverseRelations and `FOCUSED_CHILD_QUERY.comments` (prompt-rendering bounds, not drains), `ISSUE_DETAIL_FIELDS_QUERY.comments` and dashboard fragment relations (plan rule: do not widen the diff). They stay on the allowlist with reasons; tracked by LIN-4325, LIN-4326, LIN-4327.
